# azion_network_list (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "azion_network_list" "example_countries" {
  results {
    name = "NetworkList Countries Example"
    type = "countries"
    items = [
      "BR",
      "US",
      "AG"
    ]
  }
}

resource "azion_network_list" "example_ip_cidr" {
  results {
    name = "NetworkList IP CIDR Example"
    type = "ip_cidr"
    items = [
      "192.168.0.1",
      "192.168.0.2",
      "192.168.0.3"
    ]
  }
}

resource "azion_network_list" "example_asn" {
  results {
    name = "NetworkList ASN Example"
    type = "asn"
    items = [
      "1234",
      "5678",
      "13335"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `results` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--results))

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

- `schema_version` (Number)

<a id="nestedblock--results"></a>
### Nested Schema for `results`

Required:

- `items` (Set of String) List of items in the network list. Contents depend on the type: country codes, IP addresses, or ASN numbers.
- `name` (String) Name of the network list.
- `type` (String) Type of the network list. Can be: asn, countries, or ip_cidr.

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp of the network list.
- `id` (Number) Identification of this entry.
- `last_editor` (String) Last editor of the network list.
- `last_modified` (String) Last modified timestamp of the network list.
- `state` (String) The state of the current network list version.
- `version_id` (String) The identifier of the current network list version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import azion_network_list.example 12345
```
